## What's Changed
### New Features 🎉
* [feature] Update default light and dark named theme colors by @mayagbarnes in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17450
* [feature] Add `required` parameter to `st.date_input` by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17165
* [feature] Allow a pixel width on st.dialog by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17412
* [feature] Update default theme surfaces and sidebar fallback by @mayagbarnes in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17467
* [feature] Use theme primary for st.map default markers by @mayagbarnes in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17493
* [feature] Add required parameter to st.time_input by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17420
* [feature] Add per-function max_size to st.cache_data by @sfc-gh-lwilby-1 in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17552
* [feature] Add `required` parameter to `st.datetime_input` by @sfc-gh-lmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17565

* [feature] Add server.maxCacheDataSize cache budget by @sfc-gh-lwilby-1 in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17553
* [feature] Opaque default theme chrome and borders on by default by @mayagbarnes in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17495
* [feature] Send Vega-Lite selections when gestures end by @sfc-gh-lwilby-1 in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17666
* [feature] Expose the agent API to drive apps over HTTP by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17731

* [feature] Send st.echarts_chart dataframes as Arrow by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17678
* [feature] Show data table for st.echarts_chart by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17708
* [feature] Add `icon` parameter to `st.selectbox` by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17850
* [feature] Add help to st.Page for nav tooltips by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17807
* [feature] MCP endpoint for agent-accessible apps by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17510
* [feature] Add `st.grid` for responsive grid layouts by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17800
### Bug Fixes 🐛
* [fix] Add AppTest file uploads for chat input by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17464
* [fix] Make unknown container methods type errors by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17475
* [fix] Add AppTest support for st.data_editor by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17476
* [fix] Top nav section dropdown keyboard and ARIA by @mayagbarnes in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17423
* [fix] Align st.components types with runtime by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17501
* [fix] Let the default time slider reach time.max by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17504
* [fix] Let page scroll pass over ECharts inside dataZoom by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17507
* [fix] Prevent resuming a session after logout by @lukasmasuch in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17310
* [fix] Skip overflowed top-nav links in tab order by @mayagbarnes in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17482

detail.readme:
# Streamlit ### Built in Python. Made for people and agents. **Streamlit is the agent-native data app framework.** Use it for dashboards, forecasting apps, workflow apps, and any other app built around your data. [![PyPI downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/streamlit?label=PyPI%20downloads)](https://pypi.org/project/streamlit/) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/streamlit/streamlit?style=flat)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/stargazers) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/LICENSE) Each app is plain Python, written by you or your coding agent, with no separate frontend or API layer. Streamlit is batteries-included and takes care of the hard parts: a consistent, well-designed interface, state, caching, sign-in, theming, and upgrades. Your team keeps only its own logic, written in a language it already reads every day. **The No. 1 Python framework for data apps and dashboards.** [More than a million repositories](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/network/dependents) on GitHub depend on it. Used by millions. Trusted by thousands of companies, from startups to global enterprises. ## What teams build
DASHBOARDS
KPI dashboards with drill-down and cross-filtering
Revenue, product metrics, and operating dashboards that stay fast over large data. Coming from a BI tool? Move your dashboards to Streamlit, and modernize them on the way.
Try the live demo → 		FORECASTING APPS
Simulations and models with what-if levers
Forecasts, scenario planning, pricing and demand simulators, and risk models. The computation and the interface are the same Python.
Try the live demo → 		WORKFLOW APPS
Review queues, approvals, sign-offs, and writeback
Approve what an AI agent proposes, sign off on a forecast, or triage data quality. Editable tables (st.data_editor) and forms put the decision in the same app as the data.
Try the live demo →
The source for all three is in [streamlit/demos](https://github.com/streamlit/demos). Streamlit is also great for [AI chat and agent apps](https://streamlit.io/generative-ai) over your data (`st.chat_input`, `st.write_stream`, `st.status`), ML and model tools, and internal data tools. For more ideas, see [the apps each team asks for](https://streamlit.io/use-cases), from finance to supply chain. ## Get started ```bash pip install streamlit ``` ### Build with your coding agent Run [`streamlit skills`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/cli/skills) in your project folder. It installs our expert skills for Claude Code and any agent that reads the shared `.agents` skills folder, matched to your Streamlit version. So your agent follows current best practices instead of whatever it memorized two versions ago. Then ask, and mention Streamlit so the agent picks up the skills (in Claude Code, `/developing-with-streamlit` works too): > Build a Streamlit app that forecasts demand from `sales.csv`, with what-if levers for > price and growth. ### Or write it yourself Here's a complete app: a demand forecast that planners can adjust and submit for sign-off. Save it as `streamlit_app.py` and run `streamlit run streamlit_app.py`: ```python import sqlite3 import numpy as np import pandas as pd import streamlit as st st.title("Demand plan") @st.cache_data def load_actuals() -> pd.DataFrame: # Swap in your own query, e.g. st.connection("snowflake").query("...") months = pd.date_range("2025-01-01", periods=12, freq="MS") units = 1_000 + 40 * np.arange(12) + np.random.default_rng(0).normal(0, 50, 12) return pd.DataFrame({"month": months, "actual": units.round()}) actuals = load_actuals() growth = st.slider("Monthly growth (%)", -5.0, 10.0, 2.0, step=0.5) months = pd.date_range("2026-01-01", periods=6, freq="MS") baseline = actuals["actual"].iloc[-1] * (1 + growth / 100) ** np.arange(1, 7) forecast = pd.DataFrame({"month": months, "forecast": baseline.round()}) # Planners edit the forecast, and the chart follows plan = st.data_editor(forecast, disabled=["month"], hide_index=True) st.line_chart(pd.concat([actuals, plan]), x="month") if st.button("Submit for sign-off", type="primary"): with sqlite3.connect("plans.db") as db: # Or your warehouse plan.to_sql("plans", db, if_exists="append", index=False) st.success(f"Submitted {len(plan)} months for sign-off.") ``` ## Why Streamlit **Generating an app is cheap. Owning it isn't.** An agent can write a React frontend, a Python backend, and the API between them in an afternoon. Then someone has to review all three, keep them in sync, and patch them for years. With Streamlit, it's one layer of Python, and the plumbing is our job. See [how it compares](https://streamlit.io/why-streamlit) to custom stacks and BI tools. - **Made for data.** Hand a pandas, Polars, Snowpark, or PySpark dataframe straight to a table or chart. Tables load rows as you scroll, so they stay fast on large data. Native charts cover nearly every visualization, from KPI sparklines to maps and diagrams, and ECharts, Altair, and built-in charts switch to faster rendering on their own as the data grows. - **Fast dashboards.** Wrap a section in `@st.fragment`, and only that section reruns when people use it. Cached queries can refresh in the background (`@st.cache_data(ttl=..., refresh_mode="background")`), so nobody waits on a stale query. Chart and table selections (`on_select`) let people cross-filter and drill down, and filters bound to the URL (`bind="query-params"`) make every view shareable. - **Free on the logic. Opinionated on the design.** Write any logic you like, with any Python library. The look comes from Streamlit: native charts, tables, and filters, styled by one [brand theme](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/theming) that all your apps share. App number 200 looks like it belongs with app number one, no matter who, or what, built it. - **Stable for years.** Breaking changes are extremely rare. Most apps written years ago still run on the latest release, and every upgrade brings them new features, speed, and security fixes. - **Built for agents.** Agents drive the running app without a browser, read the numbers back as data, and leave tests behind for CI ([`AppTest`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/app-testing)). And every app is also a tool: Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any other MCP client can use it with the same logic and access rules as a person in the browser. There's no second API to build. More in [Streamlit for agents](https://streamlit.io/agents). - **Enterprise-ready.** Sign-in is built in (`st.login`), and security scans run on every change, with fixes in regular releases. Streamlit targets WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA for its commands and default themes, and publishes an [ongoing audit](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/wiki/accessibility-wcag.md), known gaps included. Run it in your own cloud, on [Community Cloud](https://streamlit.io/cloud), or natively [inside Snowflake](https://docs.streamlit.io/deploy/snowflake). More in [Streamlit for the enterprise](https://streamlit.io/enterprise). - **Escape hatches.** Need a bespoke screen? Drop in a [custom component](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/custom-components/components-v2) written in React or anything else. Need a webhook or your own API route? Add it with [`st.App`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/server/st.app). ## Community Cloud Deploy, manage, and share your apps for free on [Community Cloud](https://streamlit.io/cloud). Connect a GitHub repository, pick your app file, and your app gets its own `streamlit.app` URL. [Sign up here](https://share.streamlit.io/signup). ## Resources - [Docs](https://docs.streamlit.io) to learn how Streamlit works - [Community forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io) for questions and help - [Blog](https://blog.streamlit.io) for tips from developers and creators - [Components](https://streamlit.io/components) to extend Streamlit ## Contribute Thanks for your interest in helping improve Streamlit! We have paused accepting pull requests from outside the Streamlit maintainer team. You can still make a valuable contribution by [reporting bugs](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml), [requesting features](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml), [improving or upvoting existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc), [commenting on open specs](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3Achange%3Aspec), creating [custom components](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/custom-components/components-v2), and contributing to [streamlit-extras](https://github.com/arnaudmiribel/streamlit-extras). Read our [contribution guide](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md) for details. ## License Streamlit is completely free and open-source and licensed under the [Apache 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) license.
